name: Bilateral Massive Adrenal Hemorrhage

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Bilateral Massive Adrenal Hemorrhage

criteria.description: Radiological evidence of bilateral adrenal gland enlargement with hemorrhagic features on CT or MRI
Acute onset of adrenal insufficiency symptoms including hypotension, abdominal pain, and electrolyte abnormalities
Biochemical evidence of adrenal insufficiency such as hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, and low cortisol levels
Presence of predisposing factors such as sepsis, coagulopathy, or anticoagulant therapy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of radiological confirmation plus clinical and laboratory evidence of adrenal insufficiency
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other causes of adrenal enlargement and insufficiency.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Acute adrenal insufficiency with refractory hypotension
pathognomonic.notes: Severe hypotension unresponsive to fluids and vasopressors
searchTerms: sudden adrenal failure with low blood pressure
acute adrenal crisis with resistant hypotension

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bilateral adrenal gland enlargement with hemorrhagic necrosis
searchTerms: both adrenal glands swollen with bleeding
enlarged adrenal glands with tissue death

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe hyponatremia secondary to adrenal failure
pathognomonic.notes: Electrolyte imbalance due to mineralocorticoid deficiency
searchTerms: very low blood sodium from adrenal failure
severe hyponatremia due to adrenal problems

common.symptomName: Sudden onset severe abdominal or flank pain
common.notes: Often localized to the upper abdomen or back
searchTerms: sudden severe belly or side pain

common.symptomName: Fever associated with systemic inflammatory response
common.notes: May indicate underlying sepsis or hemorrhagic stress
searchTerms: high temperature with systemic inflammatory signs

common.notes: Common gastrointestinal symptoms in adrenal crisis

searchTerms: elevated blood potassium due to hormone deficiency

occasional.notes: May result from electrolyte disturbances or hypotension
Low blood glucose due to cortisol deficiency
May occur in chronic adrenal insufficiency but less common in acute hemorrhage
May be secondary to shock or metabolic acidosis

rare.notes: May be a precipitating factor or complication

rare.symptomName: Seizures secondary to severe electrolyte imbalance
searchTerms: seizures caused by severe electrolyte problems

imaging: Bilateral adrenal gland enlargement with heterogeneous high-density areas on CT
MRI showing adrenal hemorrhage with characteristic signal changes
Ultrasound may show enlarged hypoechoic adrenal glands
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; may be associated with underlying coagulopathies
other: History of sepsis, anticoagulant use, trauma, or coagulopathy as predisposing factors

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of hemorrhagic features on imaging

references: Bancos I, Hahner S, Tomlinson J, Arlt W. Diagnosis and management of adrenal hemorrhage. Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol. 2015 Sep;3(9): 757-67.
Marti JL, Grant CS, van Heerden JA, et al. Bilateral massive adrenal hemorrhage: etiology and clinical course. Mayo Clin Proc. 1994;69(6): 541-7.
Waterhouse-Friderichsen syndrome: a review of pathophysiology and clinical features. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2020;105(2): e1-e10.
